bites.title: GGUF, AWQ, GPTQ
bites.body:
GGUF, AWQ, and GPTQ are popular file formats and quantisation methods used to package compressed language models for inference. GGUF is designed for flexible CPU and Apple silicon execution, whereas AWQ and GPTQ target fast low-bit inference on dedicated graphics cards.

It is like choosing between a versatile hybrid car for city errands and a specialised track car built solely for paved racing circuits.

Because open-source tooling evolves rapidly, you should check the current details for your serving engine before committing a client pipeline to a single weight format.
bites.sourceNote: Drafted by AI, November 2026 · fast-moving topic, check current details · confidence: medium

questions.prompt: Which quantisation format is primarily designed for running models across CPUs and Apple silicon laptops?

choices.text: AWQ
GPTQ
GGUF
SafeTensors FP32

questions.explanation: GGUF was built for the llama.cpp ecosystem to run efficiently on consumer CPUs, unified memory Macs, and mixed CPU-GPU setups.

bites.title: Quality loss measurement
bites.body:
Measuring quality loss after quantisation means comparing the compressed model against the original full-precision model across general language benchmarks and domain-specific tests. Researchers often start with perplexity, which measures how surprised a model is by a reference text, alongside accuracy scores on structured tasks.

It is like testing a compressed audio file both with laboratory frequency equipment and by having musicians listen for muffled instruments.

However, mild perplexity changes can hide severe drops in strict formatting, coding, or maths, so relying on a single summary metric is risky.
bites.sourceNote: Drafted by AI, November 2026 · confidence: high

questions.prompt: What does perplexity measure when evaluating a quantised language model?

choices.text: The exact number of gigabytes saved in graphics memory
The electrical power drawn by the server during peak load
How fast the network connection transfers weights from disk
How well the model predicts the next tokens in a sample text

questions.explanation: Perplexity reflects the model's uncertainty when predicting token sequences, serving as a quick indicator of general degradation.

bites.title: GGUF for llama.cpp and local use; AWQ and GPTQ for GPU serving
bites.body:
Choosing the right quantisation format depends on where the model will run in practice. GGUF pairs with llama.cpp for local workstations, edge devices, and split CPU-GPU setups, while AWQ and GPTQ integrate with high-throughput GPU servers in data centres.

It is like using portable camping stoves for a field expedition while fitting commercial gas ranges inside a busy restaurant kitchen.

Engine support for low-bit kernels changes frequently across releases, so always check the current details of your chosen inference server before converting weights.
bites.sourceNote: Drafted by AI, November 2026 · fast-moving topic, check current details · confidence: medium

questions.prompt: When advising a client who wants to serve a 4-bit model to hundreds of concurrent users on data-centre GPUs, which formats are usually preferred over GGUF?

choices.text: GGUF running solely on a single laptop processor
AWQ or GPTQ running on a dedicated GPU serving engine
Uncompressed 32-bit text files parsed by a Python script
CSV spreadsheets loaded into a relational database

questions.explanation: AWQ and GPTQ have optimised GPU kernels in serving engines for high-concurrency batching, whereas GGUF targets local and edge execution.

bites.title: Measure on your task, not only on perplexity
bites.body:
A quantised model that scores well on general academic benchmarks or perplexity tests can still fail on a client's specific workflow. Subtle degradation often shows up first in multi-step instructions, strict JSON schemas, or domain-specific extraction.

It is like hiring a translator who passes a basic vocabulary quiz with flying colours but misreads clauses in a commercial property contract.

Before signing off on a compressed model, an AI consultant must run an evaluation suite built from real examples of the client's production prompts.
bites.sourceNote: Drafted by AI, November 2026 · confidence: high

questions.prompt: Why is a low perplexity degradation score insufficient to approve a quantised model for production?

choices.text: Perplexity only works on vision models and cannot be calculated for text
Low perplexity means the model has forgotten how to read English words
Perplexity measures hardware temperature rather than model predictions
Task-specific skills like strict JSON formatting or complex reasoning can break even when general fluency looks fine

questions.explanation: General fluency metrics can mask brittle failures in instruction following, structured output, or domain logic that matter to the business.

bites.title: A smaller model at higher precision vs. a larger model at lower precision
bites.body:
When hardware memory is fixed, a common design choice is whether to run a smaller model at 16-bit precision or a larger model compressed to 4-bit precision. In practice, a 4-bit version of a large model often outperforms an uncompressed small model that occupies the same memory footprint.

It is like asking a seasoned senior partner for a quick summary rather than asking a junior trainee for an exhaustive essay.

Still, the larger quantised model may generate tokens more slowly per request, so you must test both accuracy and latency against the client's service targets.
bites.sourceNote: Drafted by AI, November 2026 · confidence: high

questions.prompt: Given a fixed 24-gigabyte GPU budget, how does a 4-bit 30-billion-parameter model typically compare in reasoning quality to a 16-bit 8-billion-parameter model?

choices.text: The smaller 16-bit model always beats any model that uses 4-bit weights
Both models produce the exact same token outputs because they use the same memory
The larger 4-bit model usually retains stronger reasoning than the smaller 16-bit model
The 30-billion-parameter model cannot fit into 24 gigabytes even at 4-bit precision

questions.explanation: Across equal memory budgets, extra parameter capacity compressed to 4 bits generally preserves more knowledge and reasoning than a much smaller full-precision model.
